After weeks of ChatGPT users being limited only by weekly usage caps, OpenAI today announced it will restore the five-hour usage limit for Codex and ChatGPT Work for Plus subscribers. Details below.

ChatGPT Plus subscribers to have five-hour usage limit restored

Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux, OpenAI's head of Codex and ChatGPT engineering, announced tonight that starting tomorrow (the 25th), Plus subscribers' Codex and ChatGPT Work will have the five-hour usage cap restored.

After reaching the five-hour or weekly cap, users can wait for the next cycle to reset their usage, or purchase additional credits. OpenAI sometimes also resets users' usage caps for free, and accumulated reset credits can be obtained through designated promotional campaigns and referral offers.

However, over the past few weeks, OpenAI had temporarily lifted the five-hour usage cap for Codex and ChatGPT Work, retaining only the weekly cap.

During that period, the company also reset users' weekly usage multiple times ahead of schedule to celebrate milestones, including the combined two (now merged) platforms surpassing one million active users.

However, as Tibo explained tonight on X:

Tomorrow we will restore the five-hour cap for Plus accounts on ChatGPT Work and Codex. I mentioned this earlier but then postponed it. This measure is necessary because (a) the five-hour cap helps us balance the load on our computing resources, allowing us to keep the weekly allowance generous, and (b) most Plus subscribers are more casual new users who tend to accidentally burn through their entire weekly allowance and then feel confused, resulting in a less-than-ideal experience. Over the coming months, we will continue to maintain the no-five-hour-cap arrangement for $100 and $200 Pro subscribers.

Tibo made no mention of any changes for Enterprise or Edu accounts, which currently use a separate points-based usage system.

After the five-hour cap is restored for ChatGPT Work and Codex, will you be affected? Let us know in the comments.
